Definition: perhaps from G5465 through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it):--brass, money.
BiblicalUsage: Chalkos is brass — and in the Gospels it means money. Jesus told the twelve to provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in their purses, and to take nothing for the journey save a staff only, no scrip, no bread, no money in their purses.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the brass in the purse is the test of the mission: go without it, and see who provides.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
